title: Mystery creature freaks out California neighborhood: 'It's not a cat or a dog'
excerpt: A hairless mystery creature has left residents of a California neighborhood scratching their heads.
content:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

It’s a dog! It’s a cat! It’s a…

A hairless mystery creature has left residents of a Southern California neighborhood scratching their heads after being spotted hobbling through their quiet streets.

In a viral social media clip, the medium-sized animal, which appears to be severely unwell, is seen struggling to walk up a driveway in San Diego‘s Mission Hills neighborhood.

“Please help me identify this “thing” (no disrespect but I have zero clue). I was walking in Mission Hills and this walked in front of me. It’s not a cat or a dog. I’m so confused,” said Dan Fulkerson, who captured and posted the video to Instagram on Saturday, November 21.

The clip has since gained over 2 million views.

The comments section was split on what the animal could be.

“It looks like a sick Xoloitzcuintli…. Look up the name- it’s a hairless dog and looks like these,” one commenter said.

“Thinking a coyote with severe mange, or a hairless cat and a giant possum got together and created this thing,” another commenter said.

Most commenters surmised that the creature is a raccoon suffering from a severe case of mange.

“I did raccoon rehab, that’s a raccoon with likely demodex but possibly sarcoptic mange,” another commenter wrote.

In a comment, Fulkerson said he called animal control after spotting the creature.

Mange, a skin disease caused by parasitic mites, can affect household pets like dogs and cats, as well as wild animals including coyotes, foxes, bears, squirrels, and raccoons.

The disease can cause hair loss, severe itching, and crusting of the skin. In severe cases, it can result in death of the animal. Animals typically get mange from direct contact with other animals with the condition, or exposure to mange mites.

If you see an animal you suspect has mange or another condition, you should call local animal control.
